name: Wonderwerk Cave early burning evidence
description: Burned bone and ashed plants within early cave occupation sediments provide a southern African witness relevant to the history of hominin fire use.

impact.note: One cave deposit that witnesses early burning; the record claims evidence rather than a changed way of life, and nothing later is known to descend from it.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.label: about 1 million years ago
date.basis: Article reports approximately 1.0 million years ago; the numeric calendar year is only an approximate chart coordinate.

events.statement: Burned bone and ashed plant remains occur in early hominin occupation sediments inside Wonderwerk Cave.
events.caveats: Hominin involvement in burning is an archaeological inference, and the study did not identify constructed hearths; age and fire control are debated.

evidence.supports: Researchers report in situ burned materials in the early Acheulean occupation.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the cited evidence for this precisely scoped record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The researchers report fire in archaeological context; intentional ignition, routine use and any relation to other sites remain uncertain.

research.note: Initial evidence-backed admission; classifications and historical interpretations await independent review.
